mainTopic: Two people with the same name (a loan document, a found גט, the sesame case) and the wife's 'quarrel' that makes her report of her husband's death unreliable
overview: The גמרא first defends אביי, who worries that two people may share a name. It shows that a שטר חוב held by one of two men with the same name is still collected by the holder, because in every realistic scenario the document is his. Then it tells of a גט found in סורא from 'ענן בר חייא of נהרדעא'. Witnesses placed the only other man with that name in נהרדעא on that day. אביי says that even by his own view there is no worry here. רבא says that even by his view there is a worry, since the man could have travelled quickly or sent instructions, just as scribes write the place where they actually are. The גמרא then rules on an earlier sesame case: the הלכה is חיישינן, we are concerned. Finally it turns to the משנה's 'quarrel' between husband and wife. It defines the quarrel as a wife who claimed she was divorced in front of named witnesses, and they denied it. It then asks why a quarrel makes her report of his death unreliable. רב חנינא says she might lie, and רב שימי בר אשי says she might speak from guesswork. The difference between their reasons is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: Why there is no worry about the holder of the loan document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we need not worry that the שטר חוב really belongs to the other man with the same name. He would not have lost it, and he would not have deposited it with someone who has his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly should we be worried about? If we worry the document fell from the real owner and this man picked it up, the owner would be very careful with it. If we worry it was left with this man for safekeeping, the owner would never deposit it with someone who has the same name as him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier challenge to אביי by showing that the person holding the שטר חוב almost certainly did not get it from the other man with the same name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two ways the holder could have someone else's document: it fell and he found it, or it was given to him as a פקדון. Neither is likely. Someone who knows another man shares his name guards his document closely, and he would not hand it to that very man, who could then collect with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Should we be concerned or worry
Falling, meaning the document was lost
A deposit left with someone for safekeeping
He is certainly careful

phrases.english: With regard to what should we be concerned?
phrases.notes: This refers to the case from just before: a loan document held by one of two men with the same name.

phrases.english: If about falling,
he is certainly careful with it.
If about a deposit,
since his name is the same as his name,
he would not deposit it with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge to אביי raised before this section, based on the case of the loan document.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the worry does not apply in this particular case, because of how people actually behave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אביי worries about two people with the same name, the holder should not be able to collect, because the document might belong to the other man.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case there is no realistic way the holder got the other man's document, so the case does not disprove אביי.

steps.title: Even if the document was handed over, the holder now owns it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises one more possibility, that the real owner handed the document to this man. It answers that handing over a document transfers ownership, so the holder may collect either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that maybe the real owner handed the document over to this man? Then it is fine, because documents are acquired just by handing them over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third way the holder might have the document and shows that this possibility also lets him collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner gave or sold the שטר to the holder, the holder really owns it, because a document is acquired through מסירה. So in every possible scenario the holder may collect. That is why this case proves nothing against אביי's worry about matching names.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed over or transferred
Literally 'letters'; here, written documents like a loan document
Are acquired by being handed over

phrases.english: What would you say?
Perhaps he handed it over to him?
Documents are acquired by handing over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the last remaining possibility left open by step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Raises a possible objection itself and answers it with a legal rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the owner handed the document over, so it still was not written for the holder.
steps.terutzMaskana: Handing over a document transfers ownership, so the holder may collect in any case and אביי's view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The loan document case is no proof against אביי. The holder collects because in every realistic scenario the document is his, not because we ignore the chance of two people with the same name.

steps.title: A גט found in סורא from ענן בר חייא of נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: A גט was found in סורא, written by 'ענן בר חייא of נהרדעא'. The only other man with that name was ענן בר חייא of מחגרא, and witnesses said he was with them in נהרדעא on the day the גט was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גט was found in סורא, and it said: 'In the city of סורא, I, ענן בר חייא of נהרדעא, release and send away my wife so-and-so.' The Sages searched from סורא to נהרדעא and found no other ענן בר חייא except ענן בר חייא of מחגרא, who lived in נהרדעא. Then witnesses came and said that on the day the גט was written, ענן בר חייא of מחגרא was with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about a lost גט with a name shared by two men. It is setting up אביי's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a found גט raises the worry that it was written by a different man with the same name, so it cannot be given to the known man's wife. Here the Sages found only one other ענן בר חייא, and witnesses placed him in נהרדעא, not in סורא, on the day the גט was written.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט, a bill of divorce
Was found
I released and sent away (wording used in a גט)
Witnesses

phrases.english: A certain bill of divorce that was found in Sura
and this was written in it:
In the city of Sura,
I, Anan bar Chiyya of Neharde'a,
release and send away
so-and-so, my wife.
And the Sages checked from Sura to Neharde'a,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה עָנָן בַּר חִיָּיא אַחֲרִינָא
phrases.english: and there was no other Anan bar Chiyya
except Anan bar Chiyya of Chagra,
who was in Neharde'a.
And witnesses came and said

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהוּא יוֹמָא כִּי אִיכְּתַב הָהוּא גִּיטָּא,
phrases.english: that on that day, when that bill of divorce was written,

phrases.aramaic: עָנָן בַּר חִיָּיא מְחַגְּרָא גַּבַּן הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Anan bar Chiyya of Chagra was with us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the loan document case to a new real case about a found גט with a shared name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The facts of the case: one other man with the same name exists, but witnesses say he was elsewhere on the day the גט was written.

steps.title: אביי rules there is no worry in this case
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even though he usually worries about two people with the same name, he does not worry here. Witnesses place the other ענן בר חייא in נהרדעא, so he could not have written a גט in סורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even according to me, who says we do worry about two people with the same name, here we do not worry. The witnesses say the other man was in נהרדעא, so what would he be doing in סורא?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling on the found גט: it can be treated as written by the known ענן בר חייא, because the other one could not have been in סורא that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's general worry about matching names still stands. It falls away here because the only other candidate is placed in another city by witnesses, while the גט itself says it was written in סורא. Once the other man is ruled out, no one is left who could have written it except the known ענן בר חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned or worried
According to me, by my own view
What would he want or be doing

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even according to me, who says we are concerned,
here we are not concerned,
because the witnesses are saying
that he was in Neharde'a;
what would he be doing in Sura?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף לְדִידִי דְּאָמֵינָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case told in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When witnesses show the only other person with the same name was in a different place when the גט was written, we do not worry about him.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי still worries about two people with the same name in general. This case is an exception, because the other man is clearly ruled out by witnesses.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי changed his mind here. His general rule stays the same; it simply does not apply when the other person with the name could not have been there.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the worry about matching names is a real doubt that can be removed by clear evidence, such as witnesses placing the other person somewhere else.

steps.title: רבא says we should worry in this case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even though he normally does not worry about two people with the same name, he does worry here. The other ענן בר חייא could have reached סורא, or sent instructions to have the גט written there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even I, who usually am not concerned, am concerned here. Maybe he travelled on a flying camel. Or maybe the road miraculously shrank for him. Or maybe he gave instructions for the גט to be written there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with אביי's conclusion from step 4. He says the witnesses who saw the other ענן בר חייא in נהרדעא do not rule him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי relied on the witnesses: the other man was in נהרדעא, so he could not have written a גט in סורא. רבא gives three ways he still could be connected to it: very fast travel, a miracle, or sending instructions from far away. Because there really is a second man with this name, רבא will not rely on the witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned, we take the possibility into account
a 'flying camel', an extremely fast way to travel
a 'jump'; a miracle where the road shrinks for the traveller
he handed over words, meaning he gave instructions

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not changing his general view. In most cases he still does not worry about two people with the same name. He worries here only because a second man with this exact name is known to exist.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף לְדִידִי דְּלָא חָיְישִׁינַן
phrases.english: Rava said: Even according to me, who says we are not concerned
phrases.notes: He means in general, when two people share the same name.

phrases.english: here we are concerned,
perhaps he went on a flying camel.
Alternatively, by a miraculous shortening of the road.
phrases.notes: Literally 'by a jump': the road miraculously shrinks so a long trip takes very little time.

phrases.english: Alternatively, he handed over instructions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף לְדִידִי דְּלָא חָיְישִׁינַן הָכָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's lenient conclusion in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a second man with the same name is known to exist, we are concerned, even if witnesses place him elsewhere on the day the גט was written.

steps.title: Scribes write the place where they are, not where they got instructions
steps.stepSummary: Support for the 'instructions' idea: רב and רב הונא told scribes to write the town where they are actually writing, even if the instructions came from another town.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב told the scribes, and likewise רב הונא told the scribes: When you are in שילי, write 'in שילי', even if the instructions were given to you in היני. And when you are in היני, write 'in היני', even if the instructions were given to you in שילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's third possibility. It shows that a document can name one place even though the instructions came from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document records the place where it was physically written, not where the person asked for it. So a גט saying 'סורא' could have been written there on instructions from a man who was in נהרדעא at the time. This is why the witnesses do not rule out the other ענן בר חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: scribes who write documents
שילי, the name of a place
היני, the name of a nearby place
the instructions are handed over

phrases.english: As Rav said to the scribes,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא לְסָפְרֵי:
phrases.english: and likewise Rav Huna said to the scribes:
When you are in Shili, write 'in Shili',

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִימַּסְרָן מִילֵּי בְּהִינֵי.
phrases.english: even though the instructions were given in Hini.
And when you are in Hini, write 'in Hini',

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִימַּסְרָן מִילֵּי בְּשִׁילֵי.
phrases.english: even though the instructions were given in Shili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third possibility in step 5 (מילי מסר).
steps.raayaObject: That a document can name a place other than where the person who ordered it was standing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The instruction of רב and רב הונא to their scribes about שילי and היני.

steps.title: What was decided about the sesame case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to an earlier case about sesame and asks what the final decision was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the outcome regarding the sesame?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier open case about sesame and asks how it was decided. This line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sesame case also asked whether we worry about a possible switch, like the worry about two men with the same name. Now the גמרא wants the final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: sesame
what was the outcome about them

phrases.english: What was the outcome regarding the sesame?
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier case about sesame, not to the ענן בר חייא story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גט discussion and returns to an earlier open case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling in the sesame case.

steps.title: רב יימר and רבינא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר says we are not concerned. רבינא says we are concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: We are not concerned. רבינא said: We are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the sesame question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר does not take the possible switch seriously. רבינא does. This is the same kind of argument as the one between אביי and רבא about two men with the same name.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said: We are not concerned.
Ravina said: We are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with two opposite views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רב יימר says we are not concerned, רבינא says we are.

steps.title: The הלכה: we are concerned
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling follows רבינא: we are concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument and rules like רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry that the sesame might have been switched is taken seriously. So we do not rely on the identifying signs the claimant gives.

keyTerms.meaning: the final הלכה, the practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: In the sesame case, the final הלכה follows רבינא: חיישינן, we are concerned about a possible switch.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: we are concerned.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבינא: we are concerned.

steps.title: What counts as a quarrel between husband and wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception, 'a quarrel between him and her', and asks what kind of quarrel it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A quarrel between him and her', etc. What is the case of a quarrel between him and her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. A wife who says her husband died is not believed if they had a quarrel, and the גמרא now asks what kind of quarrel counts. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wife is believed when she says her husband died. If there was a קטטה, we suspect she might lie, so she is not believed. The גמרא needs to define exactly what kind of quarrel takes away her believability.

keyTerms.meaning: a quarrel
between him and her (husband and wife)
what is the case? how does it look?

phrases.english: 'A quarrel between him and her', etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה: a wife who says her husband died is not believed if there was a quarrel between them.

phrases.english: What is the case of a quarrel between him and her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of the 'quarrel' that makes the wife unreliable.

steps.title: שמואל: when she says 'Divorce me'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the quarrel is when she told her husband 'Divorce me'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When she says to her husband, 'Divorce me.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a first definition of the quarrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that asking for a divorce shows she wanted to be free of him. That might push her to lie and say he died.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Divorce me!'

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
When she says to her husband, 'Divorce me.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A quarrel is when she said 'Divorce me'.

steps.title: But every woman says that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: all women say 'Divorce me' in a moment of anger, so it cannot be the sign of a real quarrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words said in anger are common and do not show a deep, lasting fight. If they counted, almost no wife would ever be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone also says this

phrases.english: All of them also say this!
phrases.notes: He means all wives say this when they are angry.

steps.kashyaTarget: The definition 'when she says Divorce me'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such words are common in anger and show no real hatred, so they cannot be what takes away her believability.

steps.title: Rather: when she says 'You divorced me'
steps.stepSummary: The quarrel is when she tells her husband 'You divorced me', claiming he already divorced her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is when she says to her husband, 'You divorced me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the first definition with a stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Claiming she was already divorced is a serious dispute about whether they are still married. It is not just angry talk, and it shows a real conflict between them. That is the kind of quarrel that makes her report of his death unreliable.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You divorced me'

steps.whatToRemember: The 'quarrel' in the משנה is not ordinary angry words like 'Divorce me'. It is a serious dispute, like her claiming 'You divorced me'.

phrases.english: Rather, when she says to her husband, 'You divorced me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12 by giving a new definition.
steps.terutzMaskana: A quarrel means claiming 'You divorced me', a real dispute over whether they are married.

steps.title: רב המנונא says she should be believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the definition of quarrel from step 13. רב המנונא rules that a woman who tells her husband 'You divorced me' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should believe her, based on רב המנונא. He said: a woman who tells her husband 'You divorced me' is believed, because we assume a woman would not be so bold as to lie to her husband's face!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 13. A wife saying 'You divorced me' is believed according to רב המנונא, so how can that same claim be a sign of a quarrel that makes her untrustworthy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא says a woman does not dare lie about a divorce in front of the husband who would know it is false, so she is believed that she is divorced. If so, the wife in step 13 would already be free to remarry because of her divorce claim. The משנה's rule that she is not believed about his death would then have no case to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You divorced me'
She is believed
A presumption, something we assume is normally true
Acts brazenly, literally 'makes her face bold'

phrases.english: But let us believe her, based on Rav Hamnuna.
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the wife who said 'You divorced me' in step 13.

phrases.english: For Rav Hamnuna said:
A woman who said to her husband 'You divorced me' is believed.

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין אִשָּׁה מְעִיזָּה פָּנֶיהָ בִּפְנֵי בַּעְלָהּ!
phrases.english: There is a presumption: a woman does not act brazenly in front of her husband!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition of quarrel given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that 'You divorced me' is the sign of a quarrel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב המנונא rules that a woman who says 'You divorced me' is believed, so she would already count as divorced. The משנה's ruling that her testimony about his death is not accepted would then make no sense in this case.

steps.title: She named witnesses who denied it
steps.stepSummary: The quarrel is when she claimed the divorce happened in front of named witnesses, and those witnesses said it never happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where she said 'You divorced me in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,' and we asked them, and they said, 'This never happened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The quarrel is a specific situation where her divorce claim was checked and shown to be false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא's rule only applies when there is nothing against her words. Here she named witnesses, and they flatly denied it, so her claim is disproven. A wife who makes up such a claim clearly has a serious fight with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so and so-and-so
We asked
These things never happened

steps.whatToRemember: The 'quarrel' of the משנה is when she claimed a divorce in front of named witnesses, and they denied it.

phrases.english: It is where she says: 'You divorced me in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,'
and we asked them, and they said:
'These things never happened.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by narrowing the case of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wife who says 'You divorced me' shows a quarrel, which clashes with רב המנונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only when the witnesses she named deny it is it a quarrel. רב המנונא speaks of a claim that was not disproven.

steps.title: Why does a quarrel make her untrustworthy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the משנה does not believe a quarreling wife who says her husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for the rule about a quarrel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the משנה itself. Now that it knows what a quarrel is, it asks why a quarrel stops her from being believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that when there is a quarrel, a wife who says 'My husband died' is not believed. The גמרא now wants the logic behind that rule. This sets up two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A quarrel between husband and wife

phrases.english: What is the reason for the case of a quarrel?
phrases.notes: The question is why the משנה won't believe her when she says her husband died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the quarrel to asking for the reason behind its law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a quarrel makes her untrustworthy about her husband's death.

steps.title: רב חנינא: she may lie
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא says she is not believed because she may lie on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא said: because she lies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא gives the first answer. A wife who hates her husband might lie on purpose and say he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view the worry is a deliberate lie. Her anger gives her a reason to want to be free of him, even by false testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: That she lies

phrases.english: Rav Chanina said: Because she lies.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is suspected of lying on purpose.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי: she speaks from guesswork
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says she is not believed because she might say what only seems true to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: because she says what she imagines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי gives a second answer. He doesn't say she lies, only that she might not check carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view she is honest but careless. Because she would be happy to be rid of him, she might report his death based on a guess instead of making sure.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on what seems to be so, guesswork

steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי בר אשי is not calling her a liar. His concern is careless guessing, not a deliberate lie.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
Because she says what she imagines.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרָה בִּדְדָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 16 than רב חנינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is suspected of reporting a guess without checking carefully.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks when the two reasons would lead to a different ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to the same ruling in the plain case: she is not believed. So the גמרא looks for a case where 'she lies' and 'she guesses' would give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers from steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the reasons of רב חנינא and רב שימי בר אשי would lead to different rulings.
